entries.title: Source of truth is the source code, not the documentation
entries.decision: The two thesis subprojects (merge-tool-comparison and semantic_merge_driver) live in one private repo, and the declared source of truth for each is the source code in its subfolder plus semantic_merge_driver/initial architecture.md as the target pipeline. Everything derived — plan documents, tool-evaluation write-ups, STATUS/CLAUDE/README/ARCHITECTURE, generated diagrams — is subordinate: when a derived doc disagrees with the code, the code wins and the doc is reconciled to it (commit 6892637 did exactly that for five stale claims), and a review diagram is drawn from the code as it actually runs rather than from the target architecture doc.
entries.rationale: Declared at repo founding as the per-project source of truth, with all docs to be aligned to it; the tool-evaluation document was then explicitly scoped as non-authoritative because "Source of truth remains source code"; and by 2026-05-26 two stale claims predating the session showed the derived docs had drifted from the code, so they were reconciled with the code kept as source of truth. CLAUDE.md's designation of source code as the authoritative input is what forced the 2026-06-24 architecture diagram to reflect the running code rather than the target spec.

entries.title: Review finder agents return at most 6 conclusions as a bare JSON array
entries.decision: Each angle of a multi-angle code review is run by a finder agent under a fixed contract: return at most 6 candidate findings as a JSON array with keys file, line, summary, failure_scenario, and the final message is only the array (an empty array being the expected result when nothing qualifies); report conclusions, not file dumps, with no code excerpt longer than three lines. Angles are given an explicit method (for the removed-behaviour angle: for every line the diff deletes or replaces, name the invariant it enforced and verify the new code re-establishes it, with specific paths enumerated) and an explicit scope — findings must be actionable within the session's constraints, and untracked new files are added to every finder's scope by hand.
entries.rationale: Untracked files do not appear in `git diff`, so a diff-scoped review would have skipped the new lane and its test file entirely. The actionability scope is argued from the guardrails: the module deliberately avoids importing strategy classes to prevent loader double-registration, and the frozen-plan guardrail forbids changes to existing lanes, so a recommendation requiring those edits cannot be executed.

entries.title: Duplication is accepted rather than edit a frozen lane or diverge from the ABC
entries.decision: In the S-D detector work, duplication and cross-module private access are deliberately left in place rather than refactored: SignatureStaleCallStrategy keeps its own `_inconclusive`, its own `_declared_arities`, and its reaches into other lanes' private members (`self._rm2._run_rm2_pair`, `view._in_excluded`, `view._qualified_or_case`, the `_ipu` helpers); no shared RM2Runner is extracted and no `_FileView` helper is promoted to public. The test-side `_patch_rm2` is classified as a drift risk rather than a removable duplicate. The inherited `base_content: str = None` annotation is left uncorrected.
entries.rationale: Reusing `self._rm2._inconclusive` would emit the wrong strategy name and message; the existing declaration helpers return booleans with no arity, and adding arity or factoring a shared module-level helper would mean editing the frozen rename/text lanes, which the session guardrail forbids — so the duplication is "unavoidable within constraints, not a finding". The public-ish alternatives also cannot supply what the lane needs (`_rm2_renames` drops Add/Remove-Parameter records; `_FileView.occurrences()` cannot count arity). `_patch_rm2` patches a different method with different signature/return conventions, so it is a genuine near-duplicate rather than a droppable copy. The `base_content` annotation stays because consistency with the project ABC wins and the ABC itself is the offender.

evidence.text: Every less-fragile alternative (extract a shared `RM2Runner`, promote `_FileView` scan helpers to public) requires editing the frozen lane files, which the stated constraint forbids this session.

notes:
Density: 133 primary sources → 34 entries (126 sources promoted, 7 not promoted), about 3.7 sources per entry, below the 5–9 calibration band. This is deliberate and, I think, right for this theme: repo-conventions is not one argument restated but a large set of narrow, separately-citable rules (what is gitignored, what a commit contains, where a doc lives, how a review agent is briefed, what a plan file owns). Merging further would have produced entries like "git hygiene" that a reader could not act on. Where the same position genuinely recurred I merged hard — gitignore-regenerable-keep-evidence folds seven applications of one rule, push-only-on-instruction-after-review folds six, handoff-through-committed-artifacts six.

Judgment calls S10z should check:
(1) one-branch-one-pr-per-phase is marked superseded by commit-directly-to-main. The two plan-era sources explicitly require a branch and PR per phase; the three transcript-era sources explicitly commit direct to main citing the #29/#30 convention. I kept the surviving half of the older rule (small, ordered, green commits) as its own adopted entry so the supersession does not swallow it.
(2) a:ce56e78d-14 was extracted status=open ("commit the 28 MB raw_results.json or gitignore it"). I folded it into large-result-caches-committed-as-evidence because the same day's checkpoint session (a:fb0fa5c5-06) answered it for the same file — hold the partial, commit the final. If S10z disagrees that this counts as resolution, the honest fallback is to split it back out as an open entry.
(3) Two entries deliberately carry a source extraction marked "proposed" into an adopted entry, in both cases because a later in-slice source shows the thing landed: pytest testpaths (a:ce56e78d-13 → a:7b3b2669-08, commit c9ca9f8) and strategy selection in YAML (preB:pre-architecture-refmerge-21 → preA:pre-commits-13, commit 044051f). The unconfirmed half of the latter (populating requirements.txt) is flagged in the decision text rather than asserted.
(4) Plan-status downgrades applied as instructed: strategy-addition-conventions and adapter-phases-add-only-new-files stay proposed despite being stated in a settled voice, and strategy-addition-conventions carries the counter-evidence (the 2026-06-24 review found the .sc query file unwired and the query inline) in its status_note.
(5) Several entries needed actors_note because a rule set by Ali was then applied repeatedly by Claude (gitignore, caches, push gate, source of truth). I attributed the entry to whoever made the originating call and explained the split rather than taking a majority.
